The second major area of focus was related to employee engagement and HCPS employee feedback. First, a comprehensive review of the research literature on employee engagement in public K-12 settings was conducted.

That literature review is included in the report, and it was the basis of additional work around employee engagement that happened throughout the summer. We examined staff responses to 10 questions related to employee relationships, professional growth opportunities, and staff recognition. HCPS then created and administered a new survey to all HCPS employees that focused on staff efficacy, feedback structures, recognition efforts, and areas for improvement.

Finally, we facilitated 21 successful focus groups throughout the summer, each specific to different employee types. focus groups permitted a deeper and more nuanced conversation on those same topics with a much smaller group of employees. The new survey was administered over a three-week period and was available in both English and Spanish online and via paper copies. The complete survey analysis is in the report and includes response rates and responses to each question broken down by employee type. A complete analysis of the survey results is included, like I said in that appendix. Overall, 80% of respondents expressed satisfaction with engagement, which was

defined as how committed and involved staff feel with their work, school or department, and the school division. It encompasses feelings about their jobs, their co-workers, and the overall work environment. Additionally, a majority of staff indicated that their ideas have an impact on their department or school, but that number was much lower when they considered the impact that they're having on division-level decision-making. The survey went on to ask respondents specifically about feedback structures within HCPS. While 66% noted that they're asked for their input on

decisions impacting their work, and the majority believe that there is a supportive atmosphere for providing feedback, only 42% reported being aware of structured feedback opportunities. Additionally, staff requested more frequent and varied types of feedback channels.

Meaningful recognition efforts are an important research-based component of employee engagement. And while staff reported feeling valued for their expertise and supported in their professional development, they consistently noted the need for additional recognition, and this was true across all employee groups.

Finally, survey respondents were asked what areas of their employment with HCPS they believe needs improvement. Contractual matters were chosen by 60% of respondents who then received a series of additional questions about what within that topic they're most concerned about.

Compensation rose to the top with environment and resources coming in second behind compensation. The complete survey analysis includes very detailed results about those rankings and the breakdowns by different employee groups.
More than 160 participants were a part of our 21 focus groups this summer. There were 22 sessions offered, 21 were successful.

As in the survey, participants consistently noted their ability to provide meaningful impact input to their direct supervisors, but articulated the need for additional types of recognition in an ongoing manner.

But generally, under the new law in Virginia, governing bodies, including school boards, may, if they elect to, adopt by resolution the intent to bargain collectively with their employees.
This has looked a little bit different in all of the divisions that we talked to. All of them ultimately end up with a Collective Bargaining Resolution, or CBR, that's referenced with that acronym.

And those CBRs generally lay out the terms by which elections can take place, whereby entities can come forward, one entity, multiple entities who want to represent different bargaining units or groups of employees within the division.

Once that resolution is adopted, then that kind of frees up the opportunity for those elections to take place under the terms that are agreed to in that CBR.
